title: 82nd Airborne down; battalions moving off
text: 1500. First lift of 82nd Abn Div landed 1308-1400: about 7,250 parachutists, the 376th's pack howitzers and A/80th AA with 8 x 57-mm. 508 PIR 90 per cent assembled on DZ T and moving off; opposition light.

title: Division plan: bridges, heights, landing zones
text: Orders stand: 504th to take the Grave bridge and the Maas-Waal canal bridges; 505th to hold Groesbeek and the Mook-Riethorst line facing the Reichswald; 508th to take the heights at Berg en Dal and De Ploeg and hold LZ T for tomorrow's gliders. The Nijmegen road bridge to be tried once the high ground is secure.

title: Henke alarms the Nijmegen garrison
text: Oberst Henke has alarmed every ground unit in Nijmegen: a weak NCO-school company, about three Landesschützen companies, railway-guard and police-reservist companies, and 4./s.Flak-Abt. 572 round the bridges. HG company Runge is passing through the city this afternoon.

title: Henke: close defence of the bridges
text: Henke's plan: close defence round the south ends of both Waal bridges, strongpoints at the Keizer Karelplein and the Keizer Lodewijkplein, and an outpost screen in front.

title: 1st Para Bde moves off for the bridge
text: 1500. 2 PARA moves off from the RV on DZ X by LION, the river road through Heelsum and Heveadorp; 3 PARA by TIGER along the Utrechtseweg. Opposition light so far.

title: Brigade orders: the road bridge first
text: 1st Para Bde to take and hold the road bridge (first priority) and the pontoon bridge, and put one company on the south bank. Routes LION (2 Para), TIGER (3 Para), LEOPARD (1 Para); Recce Sqn to try a jeep coup de main. 1st Airlanding Bde to hold the zones for tomorrow's second lift.

title: E/504 fights for the south end at Grave
text: Afternoon. Lt Thompson's platoon of E/504 works down the drainage ditches, knocks out the south-west flak tower with a bazooka and turns its 20-mm on the far tower. Demolition wires cut.

title: Krafft's line closes at Wolfheze
text: 1530. Btl. Krafft's blocking line complete from the railway at Wolfheze south to the Utrechtseweg, HQ at the Hotel Wolfheze; 9. Kp up from Arnhem. It does not cover the Amsterdamseweg or the river road.

title: 504th: Grave from both ends, canal bridges
text: 504 PIR to take the Grave bridge from both ends, E Co from the south bank; 1/504's companies to seize the canal bridges at Heumen, Malden and Hatert; 3/504 in regimental reserve on DZ O.

title: Mook railway bridge blown
text: Afternoon. The railway bridge over the Maas at Mook goes up moments before an American patrol reaches it.

title: Bittrich: Frundsberg to Nijmegen
text: About 1600. II SS-Panzerkorps orders the 10th SS to Nijmegen by way of Arnhem. SS-Pz.Aufkl.Abt. 9 (Gräbner) attached and sent ahead to reconnoitre to Nijmegen.

title: Recce Sqn ambushed; coup de main off
text: About 1600. C Troop ambushed on the Johannahoeveweg just east of Wolfheze; 2 jeeps lost, about 7 killed and 4 captured. Squadron withdraws; the coup de main is abandoned.

title: Malden canal bridge blown
text: About 1615 (time uncertain). The Malden bridge over the Maas-Waal canal is blown as a 1/504 company comes in sight.

title: KG Möller deploys at Den Brink
text: 1630. KG Möller (SS-Pz.Pi.Btl. 9, 60-80 men, 2 half-tracks, flamethrowers) reaches Arnhem, comes under fire on the Utrechtseweg east of Den Brink and deploys there.

title: 'Bridge 11 is ours'
text: 1650. 2/504 reports the Grave bridge held at both ends; the north end was taken easily. The Maas crossing for XXX Corps is secure.

title: Spindler: block west of Arnhem
text: About 1700. Spindler ordered west from Dieren with his gunners of SS-Pz.Art.Rgt. 9, fighting as infantry, to block the British west of the town and take over the 9th SS units there.

title: Gräbner across the Arnhem bridge
text: About 1700 (1800 German time). SS-Pz.Aufkl.Abt. 9, about 30 armoured cars and half-tracks, crosses the Arnhem road bridge southbound for Nijmegen. No British yet at the bridge.

title: Model: Feldt to hold Nijmegen
text: Model orders Gen.d.Kav. Feldt (Korps Feldt, Wehrkreis VI) to hold Nijmegen. 406. Division z.b.V. is being mobilised from a static HQ in about six hours.

title: 3 Para held at the Bilderberg
text: 1630-1715. B Coy 3 PARA shoots up a German staff car at the Wolfhezerweg crossroads; the general in it is killed. Leading 6-pdr knocked out by an SP gun; battalion held in the Bilderberg woods by Krafft's men.

title: Generalmajor Kussin killed
text: About 1715. Genmaj. Kussin, Feldkommandant Arnhem, visits Krafft at the Hotel Wolfheze and is killed minutes later at the Utrechtseweg junction. Local command disrupted.

title: Bittrich: 9th SS to take Arnhem
text: 1730. Bittrich orders the 9th SS to occupy Arnhem and destroy the airborne force west of it; Model confirms. Harzer's alarm units to block the British from the north and east.

title: 1 Para blocked on the Amsterdamseweg
text: 1700-1800. R Coy 1 PARA hit at 675820 and loses about half. Battalion blocked from the Amsterdamseweg by '5 tanks and approx 15 half-tracks' moving west.

title: Oosterbeek railway bridge blown
text: About 1800. The centre span of the railway bridge at Oosterbeek goes up as C Coy 2 PARA closes on it.

title: Heumen lock bridge taken intact
text: About 1800. B/1/504 keeps the Heumen lock bridge under fire so it cannot be blown; the island garrison and its old Soviet 75-mm overcome. Bridge taken intact.

title: Gavin: 1/508 into Nijmegen tonight
text: About 1800. Gavin finds 1/508 has not yet moved on Nijmegen and orders an attack on the road bridge tonight.

title: Riethorst attack fails
text: Evening. A force of somewhat more than company strength attacks the Americans at Riethorst and is beaten off by nightfall with heavy losses. Oberstleutnant Harnisch of the Wehrkreis VI pioneers killed in his staff car at Plasmolen.

title: Sunset
text: 1847 sunset; last light 1941. New moon; the moon sets at 1913. Dark until about 0520.

title: Ersatz-Btl. 6 arriving
text: Evening. Three companies of trainees of Ersatz-Bataillon 6, sent from Wehrkreis VI on Model's orders, arriving in Nijmegen. By late evening about 1,000 men in the city (Tieke: about 750 older men plus flak).

title: Bridge to be held for the counter-attack
text: The road bridge is not to be blown; Model wants the bridges for a counter-attack. No unit has been ordered to the bridge in time.

title: Hatert canal bridge blown
text: 1940. The Hatert bridge over the Maas-Waal canal is blown as a 1/504 company arrives after a 3-mile march. West side seized.

title: 1/508 sets off for the road bridge
text: 2000-2030. A and B Cos 1/508 leave De Ploeg for Nijmegen; C Co stays. A platoon of C Co and the S-2 section went in earlier by another route. 2/508 on objective at De Hut 2030.

title: Gräbner: the danger is at Arnhem
text: Evening. Gräbner's scouts report Nijmegen and both Waal bridges in German hands. Gräbner judges the bigger threat lies at Arnhem and takes the battalion back, leaving a few armoured cars at the Waal bridge and some cars and men at Elst.

title: 2 Para at the bridge
text: About 2000. A Coy 2 PARA reaches the north end of the Arnhem road bridge (times given range 1930-2030). B Coy cleared Den Brink; C Coy trapped in the town.

title: British at the north ramp
text: About 2000. The few bridge guards in the bunker at the north end open fire and are silenced by PIAT and flamethrower. 3./SS-PGR 21 arrives near the Eusebius church and makes first contact.

title: Grayburn's attack on the south end fails
text: 2045. Lt Grayburn's platoon tries to rush the bridge to the south end and is driven back.

title: Harzer: destroy the British north of the Rhine
text: About 2100. Harzer is ordered to destroy all British forces north of the Nederrijn.

title: Frost: hold the north end
text: Bridge force to hold the north end facing west and north-west, and try to get a party over to the south end to complete the brigade task.

title: Pillbox burned; north end held
text: 2200-2300. Flame-thrower attack on the pillbox at the ramp sets an ammunition store ablaze. North end reported captured about 2230-2300. A boat crossing to the south bank fails: no barges.

title: 1/508 stopped at the Keizer Karelplein
text: About 2200. 1/508 meets fire at the Keizer Karelplein; an SS convoy of half-tracks and trucks arrives and counter-attacks. Parties reach the Oranjesingel parkway toward the Hunner Park.

title: SS convoy throws back Americans
text: About 2200. Americans attack into the city from the south. SS half-tracks and trucks, probably Gräbner's advance guard, counter-attack at the Keizer Karelplein and hold them.

title: Krafft to cover the north
text: 2230-2245. Krafft, now under Spindler and the 9th SS, to go on to Schaarsbergen and cover the northern and north-western approaches.

title: Model divides the defence
text: Before midnight. Model issues orders splitting the defence into three sectors: 1. Fallschirm-Armee, Wehrkreis VI, and the WBN under von Tettau in the west. Model forbids demolition of the bridges; he wants them for the counter-attack.

title: Tettau's units gathering in the west
text: Night. Btl. Mattusch fighting near Heelsum; five companies of 10. Schiffsstammabteilung on the east edge of the woods east of Wageningen; Lippert's NCO-school companies cycling in, due about midnight.

title: Adams's platoon in the post office
text: Night. Capt Adams with a platoon of A/508 seizes the main post office and destroys what is believed to be the bridge demolition control room. They are cut off there.

title: Frundsberg to cross at Pannerden
text: About midnight. With the Arnhem road bridge blocked, II SS-Panzerkorps reroutes the 10th SS south-east of Arnhem over the Nederrijn by the Pannerden ferry.

title: 1 Para: south to the river road
text: 0100. 1 PARA, less R Coy, to break south off the Amsterdamseweg and come into Arnhem by the river road to reinforce Frost. At 0530 Frost's call for help reaches it through the FOO net.

title: Spindler: a line from the road to the Rhine
text: Night. Spindler to build a blocking line from the Amsterdamseweg down the Dreijenseweg to the Rhine and close the river-road gap; an inner line to be started about 800 m from the bridge.

title: Pioneers and Euling over the ferry
text: Early morning. Baumgärtel's 1./SS-Pz.Pi.Btl. 10 and Btl. Euling cross at Pannerden by ferry and rubber boats, then on by Doornenburg, Bemmel and Ressen toward the road bridge (time not recorded).

title: Korps Feldt: attack the landing zones
text: Feldt's four weak Kampfgruppen (Stargaard, Fürstenberg, Greschick, Göbel; 2,300-3,400 men) to attack at about 0530 (0630 German time): from Wyler onto LZ T, out of the Reichswald onto DZ/LZ N, and KG Göbel on Riethorst.

title: WBN promises reinforcements
text: About 0300 (0400 German time). WBN promises Tettau more units: SS-KG Eberwein, KG Knoche, Flak-Abt. 184, a Fliegerhorst battalion, Pz.Kp. 224 with 17 French tanks and a Hermann Göring battalion.

title: KG Knaust arrives; Harmel at Velp
text: About 0400. KG Knaust (Pz.Gren.Ausb.u.Ers.Btl. 64, convalescents and recruits) arrives at the north-east edge of Arnhem and goes under Brinkmann. Harmel, back from Berlin, reaches his forward CP at Velp.

title: B Coy 2 Para reaches the bridge
text: About 0500. B Coy 2 PARA, about 70 men, joins at the bridge. About 740 men there in all. At first light Maj Murray finds the bridge not prepared for demolition.

title: Helle attacks across Ginkel Heath
text: About 0500. SS-Wachbataillon 3 (Helle), mostly Dutch SS, attacks the KOSB across Ginkel Heath with four companies up; a KOSB platoon taken.

title: Feldt's H-hour
text: About 0530 (0630 German time). Planned H-hour for Korps Feldt's attack on the Groesbeek landing zones.

title: Knaust takes over from Euling
text: Early morning. Euling's company group stops a British push north of the bridge, is relieved squad for squad by Knaust, and leaves for Pannerden. Mielke's Pz III and IV probe the perimeter from the east.

title: Mendez sends G/508 for the bridge
text: 0745. G/508 (Capt Novak) to go for the road bridge again by an easterly route round the city, clearing outposts.

title: LION blocked at Den Brink
text: About 0800. 1 PARA in contact at the railway near 715780 and Den Brink. Route blocked by infantry, armoured cars, a tank and 20-mm flak firing from the south bank. Recce Sqn under fire at 708782.

title: Germans overrun the landing zones
text: 0800-1000. Germans surge down the road from Wyler, push back D/508 on LZ T and seize an ammunition dump; others come out of the Reichswald onto DZ N. Gavin puts his only reserve, two companies of the 307th Engineers, into the gap.

title: 1/508 back to clear LZ T
text: 0800. 1/508 ordered back from Nijmegen to clear the landing zone; C Co to Groote Veierenberg to secure a line of departure.

title: Feldt's groups on the zones
text: Morning. Korps Feldt's groups push down from Wyler onto the landing zone north-east of Groesbeek and out of the Reichswald onto the zone south of it; an American ammunition dump taken. Progress slow everywhere.

title: Gliders put back: zones clear by 1400
text: 0840. Division told the glider lift is postponed to about 1400. LZ T and LZ N must be cleared of the enemy before then.

title: Gräbner: break through to the north
text: Gräbner's battalion, back from the Betuwe, to rush the bridge from the south and break through to the town.

title: Hicks takes command; Staffords to Arnhem
text: 0915. Brig Hicks takes command of the division; the GOC is missing. 0930-1000: 2 S Staffords (first-lift half) ordered to reinforce 1 Para Bde in Arnhem. Second lift due 1000, delayed by fog.

title: Feldt advancing; Göbel on Riethorst
text: About 0930 (1030 German time). Feldt's force advancing between Groesbeek and Beek. KG Göbel attacks Riethorst, short of strength, cohesion and fire support; its armour caught by bazookas in the low ground.

title: Honinghutje bridges blown
text: 1030. Charges fired at Honinghutje: the railway bridge is destroyed and the road bridge damaged.

title: G/508 stopped near the Belvedere
text: About 1100. G/508 gets to about a block from the traffic circle (100-400 yd from the bridge by different accounts) and is stopped by the defenders round the Belvedere. D/508 surrounded on LZ T.

title: Bridge 10 taken, damaged
text: 1100. 81-mm mortars come up at Honinghutje; the Germans withdraw and the position is overrun. About noon a 504th platoon moves onto the west end.

title: Euling and Reinhold at the Waal bridge
text: About 1100 (midday German time). Euling's battalion reaches the road bridge, the half-track company rolling over at full speed; HQ in Hunner Park. Major Ahlborn's local troops placed under him. Reinforced SS infantry retake the northern roundabouts from the Americans.

title: Euling to hold the south end
text: Euling's battalion to dig in round Hunner Park and the Valkhof and hold the south end of the road bridge. Baumgärtel's pioneers to prepare both Waal bridges for demolition. Model has forbidden demolition.

title: Gräbner's attack beaten off
text: About 1130. After about 2 hours the attack on the bridge is beaten off; 10-12 vehicles knocked out on the ramp, six by 6-pdr and four by PIAT. Bridge force losses light.

title: Gräbner killed on the ramp
text: About 1130. The attack over the bridge has failed: 10-12 vehicles lost and about 70 men killed, Gräbner among them. Survivors hold the south approach facing north.

title: LZ T cleared: 149 prisoners
text: 1400. 1/508 on its objective as the gliders come in: about 50 Germans killed, 149 captured and 16 x 20-mm guns taken, for 2 killed and 9 wounded. C/505 cleared LZ N at 1350; Capt Stefanich killed. G/508 ordered back from Nijmegen.

title: Thrown off the landing zones
text: About 1400. Feldt's northern group thrown back off the zone north-east of Groesbeek with heavy loss in prisoners and 20-mm guns; the Reichswald group off the zone south of Groesbeek. Gliders coming in overhead.

title: Second lift: 4th Para Bde drops
text: 1400-1515. Second lift arrives four hours late: 4th Para Bde, 1,914 men, on DZ Y under fire; 156 Bn jumps 1400, Bde HQ 1420, 11 Bn about 1430. Gliders on LZ S (69) and LZ X (204).

title: Renkum taken
text: After 1400. The British company leaves Renkum along the river; Lippert's NCO school and the naval battalion occupy it and push on toward Heelsum. Lippert's HQ at Heelsum.

title: Paratroops drop on Helle
text: About 1430 (about 1500 by German accounts). The second lift drops on and behind Helle's battalion on Ginkel Heath. The KOSB counter-attack and the battalion breaks: one company captured intact, another destroyed.

title: Gliders lost beyond Wyler
text: Afternoon. 385 of 454 gliders inside the lines. 19 came down in German ground north-east of LZ T; 8 of the 319th's beyond Wyler (45 men lost); a 320th serial released over Germany and not one man got back.

title: Browning cancels the bridge envelopment
text: Mid-afternoon. Browning approves, then cancels, Gavin's plan for a 504th battalion and the 508th to envelop the road bridge, because of XXX Corps's situation. No further attack on the bridge until the 19th.

title: 11 Bn taken from Hackett
text: 1515. Hackett is told on landing that 11 Bn is to go into Arnhem under 1 Para Bde. He objects, then agrees, and asks for 7 KOSB in exchange; Hicks agrees.

title: Stirling resupply scattered
text: 1515-1530. 33 Stirlings drop 87 tons; Div log 1525 'somewhat scattered'. About 12 tons collected, and 14 tons from three bulk-loaded Hamilcars. Two aircraft lost.

title: GOC and Brigadier cut off
text: Afternoon. Urquhart and Lathbury break away from 3 PARA; Lathbury wounded. Urquhart hides in a house near the hospital. Frost now commands the whole bridge force.

title: B-24 resupply on DZ N
text: 1557. 131 B-24s drop on DZ N, loads spread up to 3,000 yd; the 448th Group drops near DZ O at 1630. About 80 per cent of 258 tons recovered.

title: Div HQ to the Hartenstein
text: 1600-1700. Div HQ moves to the Hartenstein Hotel; the divisional dump set up there. 3 Bty in action by Oosterbeek church; 1 and 2 Btys move north of the Utrechtseweg.

title: Second British attack repulsed
text: Afternoon. A co-ordinated British attack in west Arnhem is repulsed. Möller falls back to stronger positions on the Utrechtseweg just east of the St Elisabeth Gasthuis.

title: Harmel: guns into the bridge houses
text: Afternoon. Harmel orders a 10th SS light howitzer battery into the gardens on the bridge approach to fire over open sights into the British-held houses.

title: Reinhold co-ordinates the bridgehead
text: Afternoon. Reinhold takes over co-ordination of the Nijmegen defence from his CP on the north bank. KG Reinhold short of heavy weapons because of the limited ferry.

title: Tanks knocked out under the ramp
text: Late afternoon. An attack from the east by infantry and two tanks under the ramp is beaten off; both tanks knocked out, at least one by a 6-pdr. Two buildings on the east side of the perimeter taken.

title: Fighter-bombers over the Reichswald
text: Late afternoon. 97 Spitfires and Mustangs of 2nd TAF bomb and strafe the Reichswald at Gavin's request.

title: 11 Bn to the bridge
text: About 1730. 11 Bn to march for the bridge under 1 Para Bde via Wolfheze and Oosterbeek, picking up its transport and E Troop's 6-pdrs on the way.

title: Polette relieved at Bridge 10
text: 1730. A 504th company takes over Bridge 10 and Polette is recalled. The damaged bridge is later judged unfit for armour.

title: Jagdpanzer platoon in Hunner Park
text: Evening (time not recorded). A Panzerjäger platoon of four self-propelled anti-tank guns in Hunner Park with Euling; Henke's companies in the Kronenburgerpark and at the station.

title: 1 Para down to 100 men
text: 1830. 1 PARA about 100 men left, almost out of ammunition, just west of the hospital. T Coy down to 22.

title: Airlanding Bde to Oosterbeek
text: 1900. Zones abandoned now the second lift is in. 1 Border to Phase II positions on the west side of Oosterbeek, 1 AL Bde HQ to the Bilderberg, 7 KOSB to Johannahoeve to hold LZ L for the Poles.

title: Siege at the bridge
text: Evening. The bridge settles into a siege: general shelling and mortaring of the British houses. No German traffic can use the bridge; the 10th SS goes round by Pannerden.

title: Reinhold: hold both bridges
text: Reinhold to co-ordinate the defence of both Waal bridges from Lent: Euling at the road bridge, Henke at the railway bridge, outposts and fire trenches in the north-bank dyke.

title: Staffords meet 1 and 3 Para
text: 1900-2000. First-lift half of 2 S Staffords meets the remnants of 1 and 3 PARA at 726776 and resupplies 1 Para with ammunition. R Coy 1 Para, about 40, rejoins.

title: 156 Bn hits the Spindler line
text: 2100. C Coy 156 Bn ambushed at 696794 on the Dreijenseweg line. Battalion forms a firm base for the night in wood 678802, short of LZ L.

title: British stopped on the Dreijenseweg
text: 2100. A British battalion coming east along the railway runs into Spindler's line on the Dreijenseweg and halts.

title: Inf.Btl. 526 marching up
text: Night. Infanterie-Bataillon 526, 350 men on paper, detrained at Bedburg-Hau today and marches to positions west of Kranenburg.

title: XXX Corps expected tomorrow
text: Night. First word that XXX Corps should reach the division tomorrow morning; the Grave bridge is ready for it.

title: 4th Para Bde plan for the 19th
text: Plan for tomorrow: 156 Bn to take the Koepel; 10 Bn a firm base at 693811; 7 KOSB under command from 0800 to protect LZ L for the Polish gliders.

title: Dawn attack on the bridge
text: 0230. New plan: 1 and 3 PARA to attack along the river road (Onderlangs), 2 S Staffords along the Utrechtseweg toward the Monastery, 11 Bn following. Start about 0400.

title: Reinhold's dispositions
text: Euling at Hunner Park and the Valkhof with the pioneers and SP guns; Henke's companies in the Kronenburgerpark and on the railway embankment; 88s at the Keizer Lodewijkplein; outposts and fire trenches in the north-bank dyke; Schwappacher's guns at Oosterhout.

title: Dawn attack goes in
text: 0400-0445. 1 PARA crosses the start line on the river road, 3 PARA behind; 2 S Staffords advance on the Utrechtseweg in the order D, B, A Coy; 11 Bn following.

title: 1 Para hit by tanks
text: 0430-0500. 1 PARA under heavy fire on the river road; tanks at 0500. By 0600 R Coy 6, S Coy 15, T Coy 8 and about 10 of Bn HQ left.

title: River-bank companies pushed back
text: 0500. British attack along the river bank; the PGR 20 companies pushed back, then hold with tanks and 20-mm fire from the south bank at Meinerswijk.

title: 3/508 attacks Beek
text: Dawn. 3/508 attacks Beek. A G/508 platoon on Devil's Hill driven off three times in the morning.

title: StuG 280 split among the Kampfgruppen
text: Morning (time estimated). StuG-Brigade 280, 7 StuG III and 3 StuH 42, arrives through Willemsplein. Spindler gives three guns each to Harder, Möller and Allwörden.

title: Probes at Wyler and Devil's Hill
text: Morning. Feldt's troops drive the American platoon off Devil's Hill three times. A truck lost to a 57-mm at Wyler at dawn.

title: Dobie captured; Fitch killed
text: 0730. Dobie's party of 1 PARA captured; 39 men were still able to fight at 0630. 3 PARA under heavy MG and 20-mm fire; withdrawal ordered and Lt Col Fitch killed.

title: Household Cavalry at Grave
text: 0820. B Sqn 2nd HCR armoured cars reach the Grave bridge and link up with the 504th. XXX Corps has arrived.

title: 156 Bn on the Dreijenseweg
text: 0830-0930. 156 Bn's A Coy, then B Coy, attack the Dreijenseweg; A Coy loses all its officers. 10 Bn held at 690810 from north and east.

title: Hold the Dreijenseweg
text: Sperrverband Spindler to hold the Dreijenseweg with armoured cars, SP guns and dual-purpose flak against the new British brigade coming from the west.

title: Assault guns stop the British
text: About 0900-1000 (clock uncertain). Möller's men with assault guns stop the British attack on the Utrechtseweg; SP guns and tanks close on the British at the museum.

title: GOC: 11 Bn to halt
text: 0900. Urquhart, back at Div HQ, has 11 Bn halted. Staffords on the defensive since 0800 with SP guns and tanks closing.

title: Grenadiers at Grave
text: About 1000. Leading Grenadier Guards tanks at Grave; diverted via Overasselt and the Heumen lock bridge, as the Honinghutje bridge will not take tanks. The 325th's glider lift cancelled for weather.

title: Column broken up at Riethorst
text: During the day. About 500 Germans moving on Mook and Riethorst from the south-west are broken up by American artillery.

title: Staffords overrun at the museum
text: About 1050. PIAT ammunition gone at the Monastery. By about 1100 B Coy overrun by tanks and infantry; A Coy lost entire; CO and 2IC captured.

title: Möller retakes the museum
text: About 1100. Tanks, assault guns and Möller's infantry overrun the British at the museum on the Utrechtseweg.

title: 11 Bn to take Heijenoord
text: 1100. 11 Bn ordered to take the Heijenoord - Diependal high ground as a pivot. Lt Fraser has about 120 men of all 1 Para Bde units at 723783.

title: The story so far
text: 17 Sep: the 82nd landed round Groesbeek, took the Grave and Heumen bridges intact but saw the Malden, Hatert and Mook bridges blown, and 1/508's night attack was stopped at the Keizer Karelplein. 18 Sep: Korps Feldt overran the landing zones and was thrown off just as the gliders came in, while the Honinghutje bridge was taken damaged and the SS reached the Waal bridge. This morning the Household Cavalry met the 504th at Grave at 0820 and the Grenadier Guards are south of Nijmegen; at Arnhem 2 Para still holds the north end of the bridge but the rest of 1st Airborne is held in the west of the town.

title: The story so far
text: 17 Sep: Henke's weak garrison was alone in Nijmegen while the Americans took the Grave and Heumen bridges; Gräbner's reconnaissance battalion passed through and turned back for Arnhem. 18 Sep: with the Arnhem bridge blocked, Euling's battalion, Baumgärtel's pioneers and Reinhold came round by the Pannerden ferry and dug in at Hunner Park, the Valkhof and Lent, while Korps Feldt's attack on the landing zones failed, leaving the 406th about 500 effectives. Model still forbids blowing the Waal bridges; this morning British armour reached Grave.

title: Krafft to attack into LZ L
text: KG Krafft, reinforced with Marine-Rgt. 642, 1. Schiffsstamm-Rgt. and police, to attack south across the Amsterdamseweg this afternoon toward the railway and LZ L.

title: Molenhoek conference: the bridges
text: Midday to early afternoon. Browning, Horrocks, Gavin and Adair confer at Molenhoek. Plan: 2/505 with the Grenadier group against the Nijmegen bridges this afternoon; the British offer assault boats for a crossing.

title: 11 Bn caught forming up
text: 1330-1430. 11 Bn caught forming up by mortars and tanks; A Coy cut off and surrenders; Lt Col Lea wounded and captured. Cain's Staffords abandon Den Brink about 1330.

title: British broken in west Arnhem
text: Early afternoon. The last British battalion attempting a flank attack is caught forming up. The remnants fall back west toward Oosterbeek; assault guns pursue from about midday.

title: Pursue toward Oosterbeek
text: From about midday the assault guns and Möller's men to follow the beaten British west along the Utrechtseweg toward Oosterbeek.

title: Urquhart: 4th Para Bde south of the railway
text: 1400-1420. Urquhart at 4th Para Bde HQ orders the brigade to disengage and form the eastern flank along the railway crossings 712784-715780-712774. 156 Bn has lost about half.

title: Thompson Force at Oosterbeek-Laag
text: About 1430. About 300 survivors of 1, 3, 11 Para and the Staffords reach road junction 705774. Lt Col Thompson of the Light Regt deploys them to cover the road from Arnhem.

title: Polish gliders land on LZ L
text: About 1500-1600 (times vary). About 30 Polish gliders land on LZ L in the middle of 4th Para Bde's withdrawal; exchanges of fire with the KOSB. Two 6-pdrs and about 4 jeeps reach Oosterbeek; 9 Poles killed.

title: Krafft attacks into the glider landing
text: About 1500 (1600 German time). KG Krafft attacks south over the Amsterdamseweg into LZ L as gliders are landing; 9. Kp's commander Leiteritz killed. By night Krafft has closed up to Tettau's left.

title: 19 Sep drop fails
text: 1530. Only 32 aircraft of the 61st TCG reach DZ O out of 167 planned. Dropped high and fast; recovery negligible, about 20 per cent officially. Division critically short of food and ammunition.

title: Three columns into Nijmegen
text: Attack plan: one troop of No. 3 Sqn with a Grenadier platoon and D/505 for the railway bridge; three troops with No. 2 Coy and E and F/505 for the road bridge; four tanks of No. 1 Sqn with No. 3 Coy and a 505th platoon for the post office.

title: Resupply falls to the enemy
text: About 1600. 163 aircraft drop 388 tons on SDP V, in German hands; Eureka, smoke and panels at Div HQ have little effect. About 12 tons collected. 13 aircraft shot down; Flt Lt Lord's Dakota lost.

title: Grenadiers and 2/505 into Nijmegen
text: 1600-1700 (times differ). Grenadiers and 2/505 attack from Sionshof in three columns: railway bridge, road bridge and post office. E and F/505 stopped at the Hunner Park traffic circle.

title: A/508 retakes Devil's Hill
text: 1600-1800. A/508 retakes the crest of Devil's Hill, losing 10 killed and 7 wounded; B/508 takes Wyler, held by about one company.

title: Attack on the bridges stopped
text: Afternoon. The western force is stopped at the railway embankment, its lead tank hit by the pre-registered north-bank battery, as two SP guns come out of the embankment tunnel. The eastern force stopped at the Keizer Lodewijkplein by the 88 and the anti-tank guns.

title: 10 Bn at the Wolfheze crossing
text: 1700-1800. 10 Bn reaches the Wolfheze level crossing, finds it partly held and digs in 200 yd south. Vehicles through the culvert; many vehicles and A/Tk guns lost.

title: Sperrlinie moves west
text: Afternoon. The line follows the retreating British west toward Oosterbeek; a StuG on the Utrechtseweg at the Wilhelminastraat by late afternoon.

title: Post office taken
text: About 1730. Thorne's column takes the post office; it holds no bridge detonators.

title: Stopped 400 yards from both bridges
text: Nightfall. Grenadier diary: heavy opposition encountered 400 yards from both bridges; consolidated for the night at Hunner Park and the Kronenburgerpark.

title: Diversion at Oosterhout
text: About 1900. Schwappacher's gunners make a diversionary counter-attack at Oosterhout.

title: Thompson to hold the south-east
text: 1900. Defence of the south-east put under Lt Col Thompson of the Light Regt, HQ at Oosterbeek church, with the survivors from Arnhem. Border companies attacked lightly.

title: Two Tigers at the bridge
text: About 1900 (2000 German time). The first two Tigers of Kp. Hummel on the bridge ramp; they shell the houses on the Eusebiusbuitensingel. Knaack's Tiger hit on turret and gun by a 6-pdr.

title: KOSB into the White House
text: 1900-2400. 7 KOSB reaches the Div HQ area and by midnight holds the woods and houses at 696791, the White House and the Ommershof.

title: Bridge houses burning
text: Evening. At least five houses at the bridge burned down, including a key one east of the ramp. Up to 150 wounded in the cellars; ammunition acute.

title: Plan for the 20th: clear the south bank
text: For tomorrow: clear western Nijmegen and the south bank round the power station for a boat crossing; 3/504 brought up from reserve. H-hour first set for 0800.

at.place: Waal bank by the PGEM power station

title: 4th Para Bde: into the perimeter
text: Night. 4th Para Bde, outside the divisional area near Wolfheze, to come into the perimeter at first light.

title: 3/504 at Jonkerbos
text: 2115. 3/504 crosses the Heumen bridge and harbours at Jonkerbos.

title: A Gp B: anti-tank weapons to Nijmegen
text: About 2245 (from the A Gp B war diary). Heeresgruppe B orders more troops and all available anti-tank weapons to Nijmegen by the Huissen ferry. A dawn counter-attack is planned.

title: II Fallschirmkorps in the Reichswald
text: Night. Meindl's II. Fallschirmkorps arrives in the Reichswald with a Luftwaffe battalion and six mixed battalions. KG Becker, Greschick and Hermann assembling on the east edge.

title: Concentric attack on Groesbeek
text: Plan for the 20th: two concentric attacks converging on Groesbeek. Korps Feldt (KG Becker) from the north-east on Beek, Berg en Dal and Wyler; II. FJ-Korps (KG Hermann) from the south-east through Riethorst on Mook. Saunders gives the goal as the Maas-Waal canal.

title: The ring closes in the north
text: Night. KG Knoche links up with Krafft's right flank, closing the north side of the pocket. Btl. Wossowski spends the night on the Ede road.

title: Dawn attack on the road bridge
text: 2/505 to attack again toward the road bridge at 0530; western Nijmegen to be cleared from first light.

title: Thompson Force: about 440 men
text: 2315. Return: S Staffords 100, 1 PARA 116, 3 PARA 40, 11 PARA 150, glider pilots 30, FOOs 2. About 438, with four 6-pdrs and a 17-pdr.

title: Kampfgruppen to attack at dawn
text: Night. KG Becker (FJR 5, 8 and 9) assembling at the Wyler-Zyfflich border, KG Hermann south and east of Riethorst, KG Greschick's conscripts toward Wyler and Den Heuvel. H-hour set for 0630 (reportedly).

title: British pushed south of the railway
text: About 0500 (0600 German time). KG Krafft has driven the British south over the railway.

title: Hackett: into the divisional area
text: 4th Para Bde to break into the divisional area: from Pt 232 by the track at 677794, the Breedelaan and road junction 683785; order of march 156, Bde HQ, 10 Bn.

title: 2/505 dawn attack fails
text: 0530. 2/505's attack toward the road bridge fails.

title: Wossowski: sweep the woods
text: Btl. Wossowski, about 600 on bicycles, to sweep the woods by Ginkel Heath, then cycle on to Wolfheze.

title: Tettau's units through Krafft
text: About 0730 (0830 German time). Tettau's units pass through Krafft's line west of Oosterbeek.

title: Clearing western Nijmegen
text: From 0800. 1st Grenadiers and the 504th, with two tank squadrons, clear western Nijmegen and the south bank round the crossing site. Lt Prescott's tank lost.

title: Crossing H-hour slips
text: Crossing H-hour put back from 0800 to 1100, then 1330, then 1500: the boats have not come up.

at.place: Waal bank by the PGEM power station

title: Inf.Btl. 526 attacks Groesbeek
text: 0800. Inf.Btl. 526 attacks through De Horst toward Groesbeek, two companies up; broken up by American MG fire.

title: Bridge: north end held
text: 0820. 1 Para Bde reports the north end held and the bridge intact; asks for reinforcements and a surgical team. The 6-pdrs cannot be manned under direct fire.

title: 3/504 warned for the crossing
text: 0900. Warning order to 3/504: cross the Waal by assault boat west of the city and take the north ends of the bridges.

at.place: Waal bank by the PGEM power station

title: Becker: Beek, then the canal
text: KG Becker to take Beek and the hills, then push west to the Maas-Waal canal. Mortar fire on Devil's Hill opens the attack in the Beek sector this morning.

title: More Tigers arrive
text: 20 Sep (time not recorded). The rest of Kp. Hummel's Tigers, about 12, reach Arnhem and go to KG Knaust at the bridge.

title: The bridges are not to be blown
text: Model's prohibition stands: the Waal bridges are to be held, not blown; he wants them for the counter-attack. The pioneers' charges on the road bridge are ready.

title: Wyler attacked
text: 0930-0950. Artillery on Wyler from 0930; a two-company attack at 0950 broken up, then a battalion-strength attack. A dawn attack on Devil's Hill repulsed.

title: 156 down to 91 men
text: 1000. 156 Bn at 682786: HQ Coy 30, A Coy 15, B Coy 6, C Coy 40. Border's A Coy attacked by infantry and an SP gun.

title: Möller's assault groups
text: Morning. Möller leads assault groups down the Utrechtseweg with RAD, naval and Luftwaffe reinforcements and assault-gun support.

title: KG Hermann attacks Riethorst
text: About 1000 (barrage about 1100 by another account). KG Hermann's attack on Riethorst and Mook begins, some hours late; three tanks with one battalion.

title: Mook front attacked
text: About 1100. Barrage on Riethorst and Mook. Riethorst held at first with ten 75-mm in support.

title: Schoonoord crossroads taken
text: About 1100. The British dressing stations at the Schoonoord crossroads fall into German hands.

title: Drop inside the perimeter
text: Division asks for today's drop inside the perimeter round the Hartenstein, not on the pre-planned point, which is in German hands.

title: Tettau under Bittrich: close the ring
text: 20 Sep. Von Tettau placed under II SS-Panzerkorps. The 9th SS to press the pocket from east and north-east, Krafft and Knoche on the north, Tettau from the west; the ferry and the Westerbouwing are the next objectives.

title: Hackett's hollow
text: About 1215. Tanks hit 4th Para Bde HQ; IO killed, Brigade Major mortally wounded. About 150 men hold a hollow at 686787 for the rest of the day.

title: 10 Bn reaches Div HQ
text: 1310. 10 Bn reaches Div HQ with about 60 men, its whole effective strength; sent to hold crossroads 705783 facing east.

title: Frost wounded
text: About 1330 (reported 1545). Lt Col Frost wounded by a mortar bomb; Maj Gough takes command at the bridge. Gough: the party can hold out till tomorrow.

title: Gavin to the Mook front
text: Gavin leaves the crossing to deal with Mook. 1/505's reserve platoons and No. 3 Sqn of the 1st Coldstream to retake Mook; the 5th Coldstream to push the Germans back toward Riethorst.

title: First resupply wave
text: 1406. First resupply wave, about 70 aircraft, over the perimeter. Many loads fall outside; 33 aircraft drop on LZ Z.

title: Mook nearly taken
text: 1410. Mook almost in German hands; the 505th's outposts overrun by 1500.

title: Containers on LZ Z
text: Afternoon. Supply containers fall on LZ Z and outside the British lines; captured panels and flares used to draw the drop.

title: Boats arrive; tanks to the bank
text: 1430-1440. 26 canvas assault boats arrive, of 32 or 33 promised. Two squadrons of 2nd Irish Guards move up to the embankment by the power station to give fire.

at.place: Waal bank by the PGEM power station

title: Typhoons, then smoke
text: Fire plan for the crossing: Typhoon strike 1445-1455, smoke on the far bank, about 100 field guns and the Irish Guards' tanks firing from the bank on Fort Hof van Holland and the dyke.

title: H-hour: 3/504 crosses the Waal
text: 1457 first wave launched, H-hour 1500: H and I Cos 3/504 with the battalion command group, C/307th Engineers paddling. Half the first-wave boats lost; 11 boats make six crossings.

at.place: Waal bank by the PGEM power station

title: Boats on the river
text: 1500. Assault boats crossing the Waal about 2 km west of the road bridge. Fired on by 20-mm, MGs, mortars and artillery; most 88s cannot depress and engage the tanks on the bank. A Spitfire shot down.

at.place: Waal bank by the PGEM power station

title: Flame tanks at Koude Herberg
text: 1500. C Coy 1 Border attacked at Koude Herberg by two flame-thrower tanks and an SP gun; the SP knocked out by a 6-pdr. C Coy holds.

title: Charges laid; surrender refused
text: Afternoon. Brinkmann's and Knaust's men work in with flamethrowers and Panzerfausts. Engineers twice try to lay charges under the ramp and are driven off. A surrender demand refused.

title: 504th on the north bank
text: About 1600. H/504 platoons on the railway embankment north of the river; a platoon takes Fort Hof van Holland. Germans start to retreat across the railway bridge.

title: Bridge: the school abandoned
text: Afternoon. 1st Para Sqn RE and 3 Para men abandon the Van Limburg Stirum school, about 30 able to fight; Lt Grayburn killed. Survivors round Bde HQ.

title: Wyler retaken; railway bridge lost
text: Afternoon. A battalion attack retakes Wyler; two American platoons pull out. In Nijmegen the south end of the railway bridge is lost and Fort Hof van Holland falls.

title: Hunner Park taken
text: 1620. Traffic circle and Hunner Park taken by the Grenadiers and 2/505.

title: Lonsdale Force burned out
text: 1630-1830. SP guns and tanks set Lonsdale Force's houses at 705774 on fire; enfilade MG fire from the railway embankment.

title: Big drop on DZ O
text: 1648-1749. 310 aircraft drop 441 tons, mostly ammunition, on DZ O, spread over about 2 x 6 miles. Division recovers 60 per cent with Dutch help.

title: Second wave: 'great rejoicing'
text: About 1700. Second resupply wave, more successful; 1 Para diary: air resupply caused great rejoicing. About 21 tons collected over the day.

title: Bayonet charge into the Border lines
text: About 1700. 156 Bn and Bde HQ break out of the hollow with the bayonet into the Border lines; 60-70 men get in. Lt Col des Voeux killed. Hackett at Div HQ 1850.

title: South end cleared
text: About 1800. South end of the road bridge cleared. US flag seen on the north end of the railway bridge.

title: Beek taken
text: Early evening. A battalion of KG Becker forces two American platoons out of Beek toward Hotel Berg en Dal.

title: Orders: a troop to rush the bridge
text: About 1800-1813. A troop of No. 1 Sqn 2nd Grenadier Guards (Sgt Robinson) to rush the road bridge; Lt Jones's sappers of 14th Fd Sqn RE ordered forward to follow and cut the demolition leads.

title: Tigers cross the bridge
text: 1815. Div log: 4 Tiger tanks and one recce vehicle crossed the main bridge from north to south. Sappers removed the fuses from the north end.

title: Armour across the Arnhem bridge
text: Late afternoon. Tigers and a reconnaissance vehicle cross the Arnhem road bridge north to south into a blocking line on the Betuwe.

title: Mook retaken
text: From about 1815. 1/505's reserve platoons with about six Coldstream tanks retake Mook by nightfall.

title: 'Tom Tit': back to the church
text: 1845-1900. Lonsdale Force ordered back to a line round Oosterbeek church, code word Tom Tit; to be in position by 2030.

title: Sunset
text: About 1843 sunset.

title: Tanks across the Waal bridge
text: About 1900 (1830-1910 by different accounts). A troop of Grenadier tanks rushed across the road bridge, losing two; link-up with 3/504 at the north end about 1910-1915.

title: Harmel: blow it
text: About 1910. Watching from his bunker at Lent, Harmel says he ordered the road bridge blown as the tanks crossed. Nothing happens; he blames a cable cut by shellfire.

title: Demolition wires cut
text: Evening. Lt Jones's sappers follow the tanks over, cutting leads and removing igniters; TNT charges found in green boxes on a pier at the north end.

title: Wounded surrendered at the bridge
text: After dark. Bde HQ house on fire. Frost orders the wounded handed over; a truce of about 2 hours and about 280 wounded evacuated. About 140 effective left.

title: Truce at the bridge
text: Evening. Two-hour truce at the bridge; about 280 British wounded carried off, mostly to the St Elisabeth Hospital. Our men edge closer to the British HQ meanwhile.

title: Surrenders on the railway bridge
text: Dusk. 200-300 men surrender from the middle of the railway bridge. 267 German dead later counted on it.

title: Harmel: block the Elst road
text: Night. Harmel orders every available anti-tank gun and gun to block the Lent-Elst road, and part of II./SS-Pz.Rgt. 10 and a battalion of SS-PGR 22 to counter-attack. First Panzers to cross at Pannerden after dark.

title: Next: clear the ramp, push on to Elst
text: Tettau now under II SS-Panzerkorps; Model orders all units round the pocket under the 9th SS for a concentric attack at 0700 tomorrow (time uncertain). At the bridge, clear the north ramp and get Knaust's armour to Elst against XXX Corps.

title: Green to find XXX Corps
text: Evening. The ferry party to take Capt Green, Adjt RE, over to the south bank to find XXX Corps. 1 AL Bde reports the ferry still under control at 1830.

title: Hold the bridge tonight
text: The road bridge to be consolidated tonight; 21st A/Tk Regt's M10s to cross after dark.

title: Gough: break out to Oosterbeek
text: Evening. Gough sends about 120 men who are not of 2 Para to try to break out north toward Oosterbeek; the rest to hold round Bde HQ.

title: Euling breaks out
text: Night. Euling breaks out with about 60 men along the bank under the road bridge.

title: Beek and the Mook line
text: Night. H/508 goes to re-establish the Beek roadblock, and is in by 2140. 185 glider pilots sent to reinforce the 505th at Mook.

title: Lonsdale Force at the church
text: 2030. Lonsdale Force in its new line round Oosterbeek church: 11 Para north of the road, 1 and 3 Para by the path, Staffords in the laundry. About 3,600 men in the perimeter.
